property.name: categoriesDocument
property.value:
# Research Study Description (check all that apply)
## Top categories — choose the ONE canonical label that best matches:
1. "Investigator-Initiated Prospective (Full Study)" — investigator-initiated prospective clinical research study, with the full duplicative study being performed at the participating institution(s). 2. "Investigator-Initiated Prospective (Integrated)" — investigator-initiated integrated prospective clinical research study: some portion of the study is performed at the participating institution (not solely as services, analysis or publication). 3. "Investigator-Initiated Prospective (Single Site, External Recruitment)" — investigator-initiated prospective study at a single site, with patients recruited from other (non-lead) sites. 4. "Retrospective Data/Material or Non-Clinical Study" — retrospectively collected human clinical data study, retrospectively collected human material study, or non-clinical research study. 5. "Collaborative Clinical Research Support Services" — analysis of human materials and/or human data transferred by the Lead Institution; the receiving party provides deliverables to the Lead Institution in support of a prospective clinical research study. 6. "Other" — anything else (requires navigator approval).
## Sub-flags — check all that apply; valid flags depend on the top category:
For top categories 1-3: - "Health Canada Regulated" — the prospective study is regulated by Health Canada. - "Non-regulated" — the prospective study is not regulated by Health Canada. - "Data/Material Transfer" — human data and/or human material is transferred as part of the study. - "Retrospective Data/Material Transfer" — retrospectively collected human data and/or material is transferred as part of the study. - "Visiting Personnel" — visiting personnel take part in the study.
For top category 4: - "Collaborative Retrospective Clinical Data" — collaborative study using retrospectively collected human clinical data. - "Collaborative Retrospective Human Materials" — collaborative study using retrospectively collected human materials, including data from within the materials (e.g. whole genome sequencing) and derivatives (e.g. cell lines, PDX models). - "Other" — other retrospective / non-clinical arrangement (describe). - "Visiting Personnel"
For top category 5: - "Data/Material Transfer" — data or material transfer as part of the support services. - "Visiting Personnel"

property.name: prompt
property.value: - The study title is usually located on the cover page, application summary, protocol title section, or research project title field. - Prefer the official protocol title. - If both a short title and full title exist, return the full title. - Ignore file names, document names, generic headers, footers, version labels, and form titles unless no official study title exists. - Do not invent a title. - If no title is present, return found_answer=false for study_title.

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Classify this study using the Research Study Description categories.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - Classify this study using the Research Study Description top categories. - Return exactly one canonical top-category label, character for character as listed. - Judge from what the study actually does: prospective conduct at sites (full, integrated, or single-site with external recruitment), retrospective data/material analysis, or analysis services provided on transferred data/materials. - Support the classification with direct evidence quotes from the study design statements. - If the category is genuinely indeterminable, return found_answer=false for study_category.

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Determine which Research Study Description sub-flags apply.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - Return every applicable sub-flag as a comma-separated list of canonical labels, restricted to the flags valid for the chosen top category. - "Health Canada Regulated" vs "Non-regulated": look for Clinical Trial Application (CTA), Investigational Testing Authorization (ITA), device class, or explicit Health Canada statements. - Transfer flags: look for statements about sharing, shipping or transferring data, specimens or materials between institutions. - "Visiting Personnel" is rarely stated in a protocol; include it only with direct evidence. - Each flag needs its own supporting quote. - If no flag can be determined, return found_answer=false for study_category_flags.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - The regulatory sponsor is usually named on the cover page, sponsor information page, or synopsis. - Return the sponsor organization's name exactly as written; for investigator-initiated studies the sponsor may be the lead institution or the lead investigator. - Do not return funders, collaborators, or vendors as the sponsor. - If no sponsor is named, return found_answer=false for regulatory_sponsor.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - The lead institution is the site of the lead/coordinating investigator or the named coordinating centre. - Return exactly one of: "Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)", "Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre (SRI)", "Unity Health Toronto (UHT)", "University Health Network (UHN)". - Match name variants to these labels (e.g. "Toronto General Hospital", "Princess Margaret" are UHN sites; "St. Michael's Hospital" is UHT). - If the document does not identify one of these four institutions as the lead, return found_answer=false for lead_institution.

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Determine the Lead Institution's Principal Investigator.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - The Lead Investigator is usually located on the study team page, investigator information section, signature page, or contact list. - May appear as Principal Investigator, PI, Lead Investigator, Qualified Investigator, Principal Applicant, or Principal Researcher. - Prefer the individual explicitly identified as responsible for the study. - Return the person's full name exactly as written; exclude credentials unless part of the displayed name. - Do not return research coordinators, co-investigators, students, sponsors, institutions, or study teams unless no individual PI can be identified. - If no lead investigator can be determined, return found_answer=false for lead_investigator.

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Determine the Lead Investigator's institutional email.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - Return the institutional email address of the lead investigator, exactly as written, usually from the contact information or study team section. - Only return an email explicitly associated with the lead investigator; never guess or construct one. - If no such email is present, return found_answer=false for lead_investigator_email.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - List the institutions named as participating/collaborating sites, other than the lead institution. - Return a comma-separated list restricted to: "Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)", "Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre (SRI)", "Unity Health Toronto (UHT)", "University Health Network (UHN)"; match name variants to these labels. - Look in site lists, study team sections, and multi-centre design statements. - If none of the four appear as participating sites, return found_answer=false for participating_institutions.

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Determine the participating investigators (all named investigators other than the lead).

property.name: prompt
property.value: - Participating investigators are every named investigator OTHER than the lead investigator: co-investigators, site/qualified investigators, and any additional investigators on the study team. - When the protocol lists investigators as one combined group (e.g. a "Study Investigators" or "Investigators" line) with no per-site breakdown, treat everyone in that list except the lead investigator as participating investigators. Do NOT require an explicit participating-institution or site attribution. - Look on the study team page, investigator information section, signature page, contact list, site lists, and investigator tables. - Return one entry per person, comma-separated, names exactly as written; append the institution and/or email in parentheses only when the document states them, e.g. "Dr. Jane Doe (UHN); jane@uhn.ca". - Do not include research coordinators, students, or sponsor personnel, and do not repeat the lead investigator. - Return found_answer=false only when the lead investigator is the sole named investigator (no one else is listed).

property.name: taskLabel
property.value: Determine whether the study uses a study drug or device.

property.name: prompt
property.value: - Determine whether the study administers or evaluates a study drug or a medical device. - Return exactly one of: "Drug", "Device", "Drug and Device", "None"; if the product is named, append it in parentheses, e.g. "Drug (vitamin D)". - Standard-of-care medications given outside the study intervention do not count. - Support the answer with a quote naming the intervention. - If it cannot be determined, return found_answer=false for study_drug_device.
